label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
Mrs. Renee, I am very sorry your toe is hurting and that you have had to deal with urgent care and trouble wearing shoes. I mean that sincerely. You have been our customer for two years, and I am sorry that when you came back, you felt I did not care. I did care, and I still do.

I want to clarify the offer I made when you came in on November 2. I offered to refund the full $45 for your deluxe pedicure and pay your urgent care copay if you brought the receipt. That offer is still open. I understand that a refund does not take away your pain or the time you have spent dealing with this. It was not meant to suggest that it does.

We did not agree on the additional compensation you requested. I do not want to turn this conversation into a public argument about that. But I do want to be clear that I did not refuse all help. You can still call me at the salon or come in so we can arrange the refund and copay payment and talk about your concerns directly.

I also want to explain our cleaning practices, because neighbors have raised questions about reused files and dirty tubs. Our metal tools go through the autoclave and are kept in sealed pouches, which we open in front of each customer. Each customer gets a new file and buffer and can take them home. We use a new plastic tub liner for every pedicure. We passed our state inspection in August 2026 with no violations, and the inspection report is posted on our wall. I know that does not answer every question about what happened to your toe, but these are the practices we follow.

Vy, who did your pedicure on October 24, is my niece and has been licensed for three years. She was born in Houston and speaks English, although she is shy. I am sorry you felt you could not explain what you wanted. Our recollection is that there was a conversation about cutting the cuticle further and Vy expressed concern about taking too much. I understand that you remember the appointment differently. I do not want to dismiss your experience or argue with you here.

I opened Lotus Garden in 2007 after working for my aunt. In 19 years, this is the first infection complaint brought to me. I take it seriously. It hurts to read comments saying all nail salons are dirty, because we work hard to care for our customers and keep our salon clean.

Marisol, thank you for sharing what you have seen during your visits and for encouraging us to talk.

Mrs. Renee, I hope your toe heals soon. Please call me at the salon or come speak with me. I would like us to have a calm conversation, and my offer remains open.
